- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.10) over recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to align with sentiment momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.20) and prices are trending down, model often overcorrects downward — adjust forecast upward to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3-5 days), model frequently overshoots in subsequent days — reduce forecast by 10-15% of spike magnitude to correct for lagged overreaction.  
- If sentiment is neutral or volatile (±0.10), model often fails to capture mean reversion — apply a mild downward bias (−0.5 to −1.5%) to reflect tendency to revert to prior 10-day average.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to underestimate true price volatility — increase forecast range by 5-10% if sentiment is uncertain or mixed.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated short-term reversals (e.g., +0.10 → -0.20 → +0.10), model often misreads trend — use sentiment-weighted moving average to smooth out noise.
